### Proxima Cen, TESS sectors 11-12 (2 min), against Medina et al. 2020

| Quantity | SetuHQ | Medina et al. 2020 |
|---|---|---|
| Flares | 61 (26 complex) in 36.6 d | 134 |
| Recall, all published flares | 65/134 = 0.49 [0.40, 0.57] | |
| Recall, published ED 0-1 s | 6/40 = 0.15 [0.07, 0.29] | |

| Recall, published ED 30-∞ s | 3/4 = 0.75 [0.30, 0.95] | |
| Our flares that are in their list | 59/61 | |
| ED ours / published (median, 95% CI) | 1.60 [1.43, 1.68] (n = 65) | |
| ED summed over our detection window / published | 1.18 [1.05, 1.42] (n = 65) | |
| TESS-band energy, ours (model ED × L from Teff and R) / published | 4.27 [3.76, 4.44] (n = 65) | |
| TESS-band energy, ours (model ED × L from Tmag and distance) / published | 2.50 [2.21, 2.61] (n = 65) | |
| TESS-band energy, ours (data ED × L from Tmag and distance) / published | 1.83 [1.66, 2.21] (n = 65) | |
| Flux-inverted null | 0 | |

Our ED is the integral of the fitted template, which keeps the slow tail below the noise; Medina et al. sum the data over the flare, so our EDs are larger by construction. TIC v8.2 has no Teff for Proxima Cen; the energies here use the CHEOPS archive's Teff (3200.0 K, labelled), and the TESS-band luminosity from it and the TIC radius. The band-energy disagreement splits into the ED definition (×1.6), our luminosity from Teff and radius against the one from the TESS magnitude and distance (×1.7; the archive's 3200 K is hotter than most literature values for Proxima), and a remaining factor of about 1.8 against Medina et al.'s luminosity, which we have not traced.

### CHEOPS M dwarfs, against Poyatos et al. 2025 (aggregate only)

Data: CHEOPS DRP (subarray) light curves via DACE public mode; Poyatos et al. used 3-s imagettes reduced with PIPE, which DACE does not serve. Targets and visits used: AU Mic 25 of 262 public; AD Leo 7 of 7 public; EV Lac 4 of 4 public; GJ 65 10 of 10 public; Proxima Cen 3 of 3 public.

| Quantity | SetuHQ original | SetuHQ denoised | Poyatos et al. 2025 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flares | 49 in 11.29 d | 48 | 215 original, 291 denoised (whole sample, imagettes) |
| Gain from denoising | | -2% | +35% |
| Complex fraction | 0.57 [0.43, 0.7] | 0.52 [0.38, 0.66] | ≈ 0.42 |
| Power-law α (above our median energy) | 2.09 ± 0.24 (n = 20) | 2.08 ± 0.24 (n = 20) | 1.94 ± 0.23 original, 1.99 ± 0.10 denoised |
| Power law vs log-normal | R = -1.50, p = 0.30: neither (p ≥ 0.1) | R = -1.09, p = 0.39: neither (p ≥ 0.1) | log-normal preferred |
| Flux-inverted null | 9 | 8 | FPR < 0.025 original, < 0.010 denoised (their injections) |

Without a CHEOPS completeness curve per star, the power law is fitted above the median energy, not above a 90% completeness energy as Poyatos et al. do; the two indices are not strictly comparable.

| Sector | Ours (S/N ≥ 4) | Ours (S/N ≥ 5) | Published (S/N ≥ 5) | Recall 3σ | Recall 1/T [95% CI] | Top-10 recall 3σ / 1/T | Amplitude ours / published |

Granulation-like background (S29): our Harvey characteristic frequencies 56 µHz (exponents 2.7); Salmon et al.: b = 150.87 µHz. Salmon et al. fit one Harvey component to an averaged periodogram (25 one-day series); we fit one or two to the full periodogram by maximum likelihood.
- Null, ar1 surrogates of the S29 residual: 0.20 false frequencies per light curve on average, 10% of 10 surrogates with any.
- Null, background surrogates of the S29 residual: 0.10 false frequencies per light curve on average, 10% of 10 surrogates with any.
- Type: hybrid δ Scuti/γ Doradus (low confidence): 12 independent frequencies at ≥ 5 d⁻¹ (73% of the amplitude), 3 below; Teff 8840 K is outside the δ Scuti/γ Doradus range (6300-8800 K).

## CHEOPS

### Detrending against pycheops (Maxted et al. 2022), same 15 decorrelation terms

| Visit | Programme | Points | Same input: rms difference (ppm), correlation | Same input: rms ours / pycheops (ppm) | End to end: rms difference, correlation | Raw inputs (DACE vs pycheops' DRP product) | End to end: rms ours / pycheops (ppm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CH_PR100018_TG035201_V0300 | CH_PR100018 | 135 | 0.03, 1.0000 | 2750 / 2750 | 1445, 0.886 | 1056, 0.9941 | 3111 / 2750 |
| CH_PR100018_TG048901_V0300 | CH_PR100018 | 227 | 685.66, 0.6863 | 648 / 1706 | 748, 0.612 | 160, 0.9993 | 583 / 1706 |
| CH_PR100018_TG049601_V0300 | CH_PR100018 | 255 | 0.52, 1.0000 | 17861 / 17861 | 14092, 0.763 | 105, 1.0000 | 21784 / 17861 |

On the same input, the linear decorrelation is the same model and gives the same light curve where both fits reach the least-squares optimum; where they differ, the one with the larger rms (on the same points and terms) is off the optimum. End to end, the inputs differ: pycheops reads the DRP FITS product and subtracts the contamination estimate, SetuHQ reads DACE's DRP arrays and keeps every unflagged point, so the detrended curves differ by about the difference of their inputs.

## What is not validated

- Flare energies on stars whose TIC entry has no Teff (AU Mic and Proxima Cen in TIC v8.2): reported as unavailable.
- GJ 1243: no machine-readable per-flare TESS catalogue was found; detections are reported, not compared.
- GJ 65: no per-flare table is public for Bruno et al. (2024); only an internal 120 s vs 20 s check.
- Poyatos et al. (2025) worked on 3-s CHEOPS imagettes reduced with PIPE; DACE serves DRP subarray light curves (about 42 s and longer), so the CHEOPS comparison is of aggregate numbers on different data products, not flare by flare. Their per-flare catalogue is not public.
- Bruno et al. (2024): no per-flare catalogue; their complex fraction (≳ 30%) is quoted for context only.
- Wavelet denoising: tuned and checked by injection on SetuHQ's own data; Poyatos et al.'s optimal parameters were found on imagettes and are not reproduced here.
- HR 10 CHEOPS frequencies: Salmon et al. (2024) publish no CHEOPS frequency list; only the TESS lists are compared.
